summary: A solid, largely production-plausible S3-compatible design with strong intra-region consistency via transactional metadata, plus erasure-coded storage and background repair. The invariants, flows, and outbox-driven CRR are coherent and would scale to large deployments, though several high-scale and operational edge cases need more explicit treatment.
strengths: Clear consistency/visibility model anchored by transactional metadata commits, immutable versioning, and an outbox pattern for reliable async workflows/CRR
Durability story is credible: AZ-spread erasure coding, end-to-end checksums, scrubbing, and repair with reasonable degraded-mode handling
weaknesses: Metadata/listing scalability details are under-specified (hot prefixes/partitions, index growth, large-bucket LIST performance, contention patterns, and schema/index evolution at billions of objects)

Data-plane and replication operational gaps: S3 Service streaming may become a bandwidth bottleneck without direct-to-storage patterns, and CRR semantics (ordering, delete markers, retries/backpressure, and reconciliation at scale) need deeper failure-mode coverage
